scene: Day 142, grey dawn over the street outside the depot. In the foreground, Patch (white round head, orange bandage above his right eye, orange backpack) leans back at the gantry rail hauling hand over hand on a pull cord, eyes wide with terror, one sweat drop. Behind him, a rope line stretches across the street from a first-floor window above a shop with a torn awning, and the woman (round white head, brown driving goggles pushed up on her head, long grey scarf knotted at her chest) hangs from a hook in the middle of it, sagging low over a street packed wall to wall with green walkers. Dozens of green arms reach up toward her feet, one of them in a ragged olive-gray sleeve. Tense because the line is dipping into reach and Patch is the only thing pulling her out.

Day 150, frosty dawn in the packed depot yard. Patch lies flat on his belly on the thin metal canopy roof, peering over its edge with wide frightened eyes, orange bandage and orange backpack visible. Directly below him, the beige coach is buried in a sea of green walkers, and through its frost-furred front window the night driver walker (green head, navy-blue two-pocket vest) stares straight up at him, a ring of keys sticking out of his vest pocket. Tense because the only way out of the yard is in that dead man's pocket.
